errors.text: The cited evidence does not address AuCoCuNiPt nanoparticles, nanoscale surface segregation, in situ heating, or the proposed Au/Cu evaporation mechanism.

The attribution of Au/Cu loss primarily to their relatively low boiling points is unsupported and oversimplifies the target mechanism, which involves surface-energy-driven segregation followed by shell melting and evaporation near 973 K.
The proposed 600–800 K threshold is too broad to recover the reported onset near 673 K.
